reasons: Both answers correct the 5% misconception, explain the distribution-based (Estonian) model, carve out the Tbilisi cafe income, and give a hedged how-much/when answer with referrals to matsne.gov.ge or a local advisor. A's full-distribution scenario is internally consistent: 15% on 55,000 of profit gives 8,250, and 5% withholding applies to the amounts actually paid out. B grosses up 55,000 as if it were the net dividend (about 9,700) and charges 5% on the full 550,000, including money that went to profit tax, so its illustrative total is slightly overstated.

B: Full-distribution scenario: B grosses up 55,000/0.85 as though the net payout were 55,000, when the available local profit is 55,000, so the profit tax should be about 8,250, not 9,700.
B applies 5% dividend withholding to the full 550,000, even though part of that amount was paid as profit tax and was never distributed.
